correctness.rationale: The leaf event restricts each independent parent choice separately, always leaving the root admissible. All surviving parents are uniform on the earlier survivors, and deleting marked leaves removes no vertex of the last-born root path. For the event probability, delete the smallest marked leaf first: its singleton probability is (i_1−1)/(n−1), and since all other marked vertices are later, none could have been its parent. Iteration gives the frozen product. The depth PGF follows from h_k=z/(k−1) times the sum of h_j for j<k (h_1=1), giving the independent Bernoulli convolution in law. The leaf transition preserves the count with probability L_n/n and otherwise increases it by one, giving the Eulerian recurrence. Expanding the product over leaf indicators and grouping subsets by size gives the stated Eulerian factorial moments and hence the joint PGF. For singleton events, summing the leaf probabilities gives (n−2)/2; the Bernoulli convolution then gives the exact transform covariance and strict sign. In a separate finite parent-vector enumeration at n=9 (40,320 trees), the two marked triples {3,5,8} and {2,4,6} had 3,600 and 720 hits, respectively, and f(x)=x² gave covariance −433/160, exactly as predicted; this does not prove the general law. The uploaded verifier was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: The joint distribution of terminal depth and leaves and the exact negative transform covariance are well-motivated invariants of the recursive-tree growth process. The stronger indexed mixed-indicator law already determines them; repackaging it as a PGF with Eulerian coefficients leaves no distinct nonroutine exact fact in this submission.
